title: Semaphores: A Counter Threads Wait On
topic: Semaphores — a single integer plus a queue: P() decrements and blocks if the value would go negative, V() increments and wakes a waiter; a semaphore with initial value 1 acts as a lock

beats.narration: How do you let many threads share a resource at once, but only up to a fixed limit?

elements.content: Many threads, one shared resource — with a cap.

beats.narration: A semaphore is just two things — an integer and a queue. The integer counts how many more threads may pass; the queue holds threads that have to wait.

elements.content: Big rounded circle labelled 'S' with the integer value 3 inside
Empty queue: 4 dashed slots below the counter

beats.narration: When a thread calls P of s, the counter drops by one. If it would drop below zero, that thread goes to sleep in the queue.

elements.content: Four thread tokens arrive from the left, one by one
Counter ticks 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 → -1 as threads call P()
T1, T2, T3 pass through the gate; T4 finds counter < 0 and slides into queue slot 0
negative value means: this many threads are waiting

beats.narration: When a thread finishes and calls V of s, the counter goes back up. If anyone was waiting, the semaphore wakes one of them.

elements.content: T1 leaves the critical section, calls V() — counter -1 → 0
Queued T4 wakes, slides out of the queue toward the gate
P decrements + maybe sleeps · V increments + maybe wakes

beats.narration: Set S to one and a semaphore behaves like a lock. Set it to N and you have an N-way capacity gate.

elements.content: one primitive — many shapes of mutual exclusion
